memory_update.text: MRCY should remain a priority underfollowed candidate for defense-qualified electronics because its product language maps directly to secure processing, RF, sensor/radar, EW, weapons, avionics, and C4I nodes.
DCO is a low-attention mid-cap candidate where radar, missile-defense, and engineered electronic-products exposure may be obscured by aerospace manufacturing classifications.

MOG.A is above the preferred small/mid-cap discovery range but has unusually relevant precision-control, missile, space, and defense-qualified subsystem exposure; keep as a large-cap comparison and possible pure-exposure exception.

For this node, primes should be treated mainly as demand aggregators; the likely chokepoint search space is Tier 1/Tier 2 suppliers of rugged compute, RF/microwave, radar/EW electronics, precision actuation, power/data transfer, connectors, thermal subsystems, and test/qualification infrastructure.

Later passes should search for smaller US-listed specialty connector, thermal, test/inspection, secure communications, satellite electronics, and RF materials names; this pass did not exhaust that long-tail supplier universe.
QRVO should remain a reference anchor for space-qualified RF/microwave and GaN/GaAs screening standards, but not the main underfollowed alpha lane.

MRCY is a high-relevance underfollowed candidate for secure processing, RF/microwave, rugged compute, EW, radar, missile defense, and defense edge-compute subsystems; later layers must test execution risk and program-to-revenue conversion.

RAL is an underfollowed precision-sensor and safety-systems candidate with defense/space, missile, aircraft, satellite, pyrotechnic, and motion-sensing exposure hidden inside broader precision technologies labels.

Need a follow-up pass on smaller sub-$1B or micro-cap exceptions in high-reliability connectors, rad-hard memory, space-grade power conversion, specialized RF distribution, and defense test/inspection because this pass selected only liquid mid-cap names plus one reference.

MRCY should remain in the underfollowed defense-electronics lane as a candidate for RF/microwave, rugged compute, secure processing, and embedded sensor-processing chokepoints; later layers must distinguish recurring production content from lower-quality development revenue.

DCO should remain in the underfollowed lane as a qualified aerospace/defense electronic systems and complex assembly supplier, especially if Electronic Systems exposure to missile, radar, classified, fixed-wing, and space programs continues to grow.

Potential speculative-shadow candidates not included due to the three-name cap: CODA for real-time 3D/4D/5D/6D subsea imaging sonar and defense/autonomous underwater situational awareness; future pass should verify market cap, defense revenue mix, customer concentration, and whether it sits below the USD 300M exception threshold.

For this node, the most important falsification question is whether the company owns a hard-to-replace qualified component/subsystem position, or whether it is simply a contract manufacturer with limited pricing power and many substitutes.
Add MRCY as a direct underfollowed candidate for qualified A&D electronics, secure rugged compute, embedded sensor processing, RF/microwave and edge mission processing exposure.
Add DCO as a lower-attention second-order candidate where the thesis depends on qualified electronic systems manufacturing, prime offload, defense/space program content and supplier awards.
Use CW as a reference benchmark for the node because its Defense Electronics disclosure explicitly links embedded compute, tactical communications, fighter jets, UAVs and helicopters.

Next Layer 1B/1C pass should search specialty RF filters, connectors, thermal management, power modules, radiation-hardened electronics, EO/IR optics and test/inspection suppliers; OSIS, HEI/HEICO, TDG, MACOM, Knowles, Amphenol, Teledyne and Viavi may be useful follow-up screens but were not included due to the 3-candidate limit.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct-public-company universe for the defense/aerospace-qualified electronics node with emphasis on underfollowed mid-cap suppliers rather than primes. Reference demand aggregators for later mapping include Lockheed Martin, RTX, Northrop Grumman, L3Harris, General Dynamics, and Boeing, but this pass prioritizes suppliers with embedded content in radar, electronic warfare, rugged processing, missile, space, and precision-control programs. The strongest Layer 1B candidates from this focused pass are Mercury Systems, Ducommun, and Moog. None are recommendations; they are research candidates requiring program-level revenue, backlog, margin, qualification, and customer-concentration verification. Expanded the node with one reference RF/space-qualified semiconductor name and two underfollowed mid-cap discovery candidates. The common chokepoint pattern is not generic defense spending, but qualified electronics and precision subsystems with mission-assurance requirements, long program lives, secure/domestic supply-chain needs, and early qualification into defense, space, radar, EW, missile-defense, avionics, and satellite platforms. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Layer 1B expansion for the defense/aerospace-qualified electronics node. The reference lane uses L3Harris as a context anchor for demand in electronic warfare, resilient communications, space sensors, missile solutions, and defense electronics.
